correctness.rationale: The repaired statement uses the same twenty-vertex graph, bit labelling, and synchronous rule. Replace tie-retaining degree-four majority by strict majority of the four neighbors and the old bit: these rules agree for all five possible neighbor counts. Construct the full exact integer successor array, seed every x with F^2(x)=x by the minimum periodic phase, and assign inverse images one simultaneous layer at a time. Induction gives correct unique basin labels; exhausting all masks rules out any other cycles. Tally by identifier and exact period. The repaired checker verified all 26 size/multiplicity rows and both unanimous sizes, and compared all 4387 triples (identifier, period, size) to the frozen table, including the checking of keys and exact row count. Among the 351 oscillators, 60 have size 2 and 240 have size 16; the unique size-8652 basin and both size-207670 unanimous basins follow from the replay. The original comparison was also reproduced separately: a fresh all-state run verified the full joint entry/period table, including that witness 64030 has F^6=917503 and F^7=F^8=F^9=1048575. It computed the symmetry orbit counts by sorting paired twin temporal codes and minimizing over all 120 site permutations and both temporal orders. Twin pairs are exactly the nonsingleton open-neighborhood equivalence classes, forcing the whole (C2)^5 semidirect S5 group. These clock and symmetry facts are not claimed by the repair.
residual_risks: The census does not quantify over other graph sizes, majority conventions or asynchronous dynamics.

value.rationale: Individual basin weights answer how likely each recurrent orbit is when the initial mask is uniform, on the canonical smallest semisymmetric graph with a substantial twin structure. Aggregate period totals conceal the orders-of-magnitude variation among oscillators and among nonunanimous fixed points. The repaired distribution and encoding-specific catalogue give a complete, independently checked baseline for that natural finite system; neither the already reported clock nor other repeated periodic statistics are used to earn value.
residual_risks: The finite benchmark is not a structural theorem for semisymmetric graphs in general.
